title: How volcanoes work
text:
A volcano is a mountain with a hole at the top. Deep under the ground, rock is so hot that it melts. The melted rock is called magma. Magma is lighter than the solid rock around it, so it slowly rises.

When the magma reaches the top, it can burst out. Then it is called lava. Lava can be red and orange, and it flows down the sides of the volcano. Ash and gas shoot into the air too. Some of the ash can fly many kilometres away.

When lava cools, it turns into hard rock. Over many years, layer after layer builds up, and the volcano grows taller. Indonesia has more than one hundred volcanoes that are still active. People who live near them watch them carefully. Scientists use special tools to measure small shakes in the ground, which can warn that magma is moving.

Volcanic soil is full of minerals, so farmers can grow rice and vegetables well there. That is one reason people live near volcanoes.
